newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-PIERCE TAKES HER TIME TO REACH ROME FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PIERCE TAKES HER TIME TO REACH ROME FINAL.

text.p: Mary Pierce of France took her time to beat Austria's Barbara Paulus and reach the final of the Italian Open women's tennis tournament on Saturday.
The tall 10th seed, who dumped American Monica Seles out of the tournament on Thursday, beat the 11th seed 4-6 6-3 6-1 after a nervous first set littered with errors.
"I started out just really slow today, I felt tired," the Canadian-born player said after the match, played in bright sunshine at the clay court Foro Italico.
Paulus also said she felt Pierce had been slow, but was referring to the length of time it took the Frenchwoman to serve rather than her movements around the court.
"She's very difficult to play against because you can't find your rhythm easily," she said.
"She takes her time and she hits very hard."

"It's not unfair because she is allowed to take 20 seconds, she has the time. As long as it's only 20. But it's very difficult. You think she wants to serve and you are standing there waiting for it and nothing happens."

Pierce, who in February teamed up with Martina Navratilova's old coach Craig Kardon, is now entering her third final of the year, against either Spain's Conchita Martinez or Switzerland's unseeded Patty Schnyder.

She said of her slowness: "It's just something I've always done. I did it in juniors. I'm not the kind of person who can play as fast as Monica or Steffi (Graf). I always find I need to take my time on a serve, not to rush."

For the first time since Monday, the stands were almost full as weekend spectators turned out to watch a player already acclaimed in the local media as the successor to retired Argentine Gabriela Sabatini as crowd favourite.

Their expectations of a resounding Pierce victory were dampened by an opening set more punctuated by gasps of disbelief as the Frenchwoman mistimed shots, double-faulted and, on one occasion, smashed into her own half of the court.
Pierce double-faulted at break point in the third game to give Paulus a 2-1 lead. She was broken again to 5-2 in the seventh game after saving two earlier break points.
Pierce broke back to 5-3, held serve but then lost the set with a return forehand hit way too long.
"It took me a little while to get going," said Pierce. "As the match went on, I got better and better."
Certainly, the second set saw a changed player with the Frenchwoman pulling off some fine passing shots and re-setting the timing of her long strokes to perfection.

Pierce was 3-0 up before Paulus managed to hold serve and break back to 3-2. It proved a false recovery as the 1995 Australian Open champion broke back and held to 5-2. Paulus saved two set points on her serve before conceding 6-3.
The Austrian held her serve in the opening game of the third set before Pierce decided it was time to finish.

In the fourth game the chair umpire overruled a decision against Pierce, to the bemusement of Paulus and the crowd who had been misled by the scoreboard that suggested there was another point to be played for in the game.
The 26-year-old Paulus, playing in her first Italian Open since 1989 before injuries stopped her career in its tracks, had not played 22-year-old Pierce since 1990.
